judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the campaign photo of the 'New In' card (img alt="", role presentation). The crop and the screenshot show 'BELIEVE' across the photo and an 'IT'S MATALAN' lockup baked into the image. The card's HTML holds only the h3 'New In' and the link 'Shop Now: New In', and no text anywhere in the snapshot says 'Believe it's Matalan'. claimTrue no: 'SHOP NOW' is not in the image. It is the HTML link laid over it, and the text around the image does say it. elementFails yes: the slogan and brand lockup are text that carries a message, not decoration, and alt="" hides them; W3C's images-of-text guidance asks for the same words in the alternative. captureDiffers no: the live HTML serves the same img with alt="" and the same overlay. Read in good faith, the claim points at the hidden BELIEVE / IT'S MATALAN text, despite wrongly listing SHOP NOW, so true positive.

judgments.rationale: A thumbnail in the #LoveMatalan StoryStream gallery, alt 'Instagram post by shopmatalan' (the same alt as every shopmatalan tile); the crop shows a woman in a black outfit beside a Christmas tree. claimTrue no: the alt is accurate about the source (author @shopmatalan, Instagram icon); it describes nothing absent, it leaves the content out. elementFails yes, on balance: the alternative tied to the image says nothing of what the photo shows. But the tile's caption 'There's nothing that a good blazer can't handle x ...' and the sibling video ('Video by shopmatalan') with an accessible description of the clip give its content next to it. A competent auditor could pass it as a post thumbnail identified by source whose content is given in adjacent text, and another could fail the templated alt, so the label is uncertain. captureDiffers no: the capture is a styled browser render with the StoryStream widget loaded; the live page serves the same widget (same StoryStream id, live channel), whose tiles are built client-side, so my automated fetch could not re-render them, and nothing suggests a different version; the headless 'Unable to play media' on the sibling video does not touch the image's alt.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: A tile link in the 'Multi Category navigation' carousel wrapping a product image and the h3 'Footwear'; name 'Footwear', href /c/womens/footwear/, destination 'Women's Shoes'. On the Women's page the link text alone tells its purpose. The other links named 'Footwear' are mega-menu items, hidden while their menus are closed, that go to the same address or sit under the Men's menu, and an aria-hidden duplicate tile to the same address; none shares its context while leading elsewhere. captureDiffers no: the live HTML has the same link and href. It meets 2.4.4, so Rampa was right to report nothing.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: [visual context] The first full-width banner link, aria-label 'Primary Banner Link' (it overrides the banner image, which has alt=""), href /c/offers/womens/offers-2/ ('25% Off (Almost) All Womenswear'). claimTrue yes: the capture has three links with that name going to three addresses, and nothing programmatic (no title, no describedby, the same 'Primary Banner' region) tells this one apart. elementFails yes: the second banner link has the same name and the same preceding heading (h1 'Women's Clothes'), and it leads to 'Exclusive 40% Off Selected Lines - Online Only' (opened live), a non-equivalent page. The banner artwork ('25% off (almost) all women's' vs 'HURRY! 40% off selected lines') tells them apart visually, so the pair fails under R1. The name also gives no purpose on its own. The third (nightwear) follows the 'New In' heading, so it is outside this set and the claim's count is off, which R1 says does not matter. captureDiffers no: the live HTML has the same three aria-labels and hrefs.
